reason: Fire the graded material to begin making the clean root bed.
expectation: The kiln should turn the regolith into mineral granules, though they may still need washing.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the nutrient solution also serves the roots, but I want the bed ready first.

effect: The kiln made porous granules as expected; they still need washing.
reaction: The porous texture makes the link to air around roots tangible.
reason: Wash the fired granules before putting them around roots.
expectation: Water should rinse soluble residues from the granules; I expect a test may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution is also needed, but washing the bed comes first for me.

effect: The granules are washed, so I can check them before using them.
reaction: A straightforward rinse; nothing surprising yet.
reason: Test whether the wash left the granules suitable for the root bed.
expectation: The cell will check material leaching from the granules, perhaps showing whether further cleaning is needed.

alternatives.reason: I could prepare food for the roots now, but want to finish checking the bed.

effect: The tested granules are ready to support roots, with nutrients and cabin conditions supplied separately.
reaction: I like the distinction between physical support and nutrition, though the test result gives no measurement.
reason: Put the clean bed into the prepared troughs.
expectation: The troughs will be filled with the clean granules, ready for nutrient solution.

alternatives.reason: The solution also needs mixing, but I want to install the bed first.

effect: The granules are now in the troughs; the remaining task is supplying water and nutrients.
reaction: It is satisfying to put the prepared material into the troughs.
reason: Mix the nutrient concentrate with drinking water; it is the only available combination.
expectation: This should make a diluted nutrient solution for the troughs.

effect: The nutrient solution is ready to apply to the prepared troughs.
reaction: The result matches the expected mixing step.
reason: Add the solution to the root bed; this is the only available combination.
expectation: The troughs should provide water and nutrients while the porous bed leaves space for air.

effect: The irrigated troughs complete the goal, and the circulation inserts explain how the two separate modules are equipped.
reaction: I like the concrete prospect of lettuce and potatoes, though I would have liked a clearer account of how the inserts give roots air.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the washed granules and seeing the distinction between root support and imported nutrients made the construction's purpose clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mixing water and concentrate was a predictable transition with only one combination offered.

surprise.text: The finished troughs include supplied circulation inserts; I had not understood those were part of the setup.

arbitrary.text: The actions had clear purposes, although the leach test announced clean granules without giving a specific result or measurement.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter to see the crops grow and learn how the troughs operate, although this chapter offered limited decisions beyond order.
